name: Chronic lower respiratory disease
description: COPD with a recorded lung function test uses the updated ADO index (age, breathlessness, airflow obstruction). Otherwise U.S. population mortality is multiplied by a published hazard ratio for each recorded condition.

layers.label: COPD: updated ADO index
layers.description: Updated ADO index: points for age, breathlessness (mMRC) and airflow obstruction (FEV1 % predicted). The published 3-year mortality per score (13,914 people with COPD, 10 cohorts) sets a hazard ratio against general population mortality for the same age and sex. Survival then follows normal ageing and is capped at general population survival.

layers.label: Respiratory conditions x population mortality
layers.description: U.S. population mortality for age and sex, multiplied by the published all-cause mortality hazard ratio of each recorded condition: COPD, bronchiectasis, asthma.

validation.dataset: NHLBI Pooled Cohorts, U.S. (Bhatt et al. JAMA Intern Med 2026)
validation.metric: COPD GOLD 1: predicted life expectancy at 65 relative to no COPD
validation.notes: Published cohort: ADO layer at age 65 with a mid-grade FEV1 % predicted per GOLD stage (breathlessness averaged), as a ratio to the same model's population life expectancy; observed: published life expectancy at 65 by GOLD stage divided by that without COPD (the cohort is healthier than the U.S. population, so ratios are compared). n is the whole cohort; stage sizes are not given in the abstract.

sources.citation: Puhan MA, Hansel NN, Sobradillo P, et al. Large-scale international validation of the ADO index in subjects with COPD: an individual subject data analysis of 10 cohorts. BMJ Open 2012, 2:e002152. Updated ADO points (Table 3), 3-year mortality per score 0-14 (Table 4), cohort characteristics (Table 1, 13,914 people with COPD).

Zhao G, Wang L, Lei S, Li Y, Li J, Feng Z. All-cause and cause-specific mortality in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis 2025, 20:4173-4190. All-cause mortality HR 1.80 (1.40-2.30) vs no COPD.

Zhang B, Li ZF, An ZY, et al. Association between asthma and all-cause mortality and cardiovascular disease morbidity and mortality: a meta-analysis of cohort studies. Front Cardiovasc Med 2022, 9:861798. All-cause mortality RR 1.38 (1.07-1.77) vs no asthma.

Quint JK, Millett ER, Joshi M, et al. Changes in the incidence, prevalence and mortality of bronchiectasis in the UK from 2004 to 2013: a population-based cohort study. Eur Respir J 2016, 47:186-193. Age-adjusted comparative mortality figure vs the general population: women 2.26, men 2.14 (2.2 used).
Arias E, Xu JQ, Kochanek K. United States life tables, 2024. National Vital Statistics Reports vol 75 no 5. National Center for Health Statistics.

National Center for Health Statistics. NHANES 2007-2018 (demographics, medical conditions questionnaire) linked to the National Death Index, public-use linked mortality files with follow-up through 31 December 2019.
